latest_release.name: exFAT Image Builder 5.1.0
latest_release.body:
Download **exFAT.Image.Builder.exe** and run it: one file, nothing to install. Antivirus removes it? Take **exFAT-Image-Builder-5.1.0-win64-folder.zip** instead: the same program, already unpacked. Check both against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## Build straight from a ZIP, 7z or RAR (#37)

Drop an archived dump on the Build page and the image is made directly from the archive. Nothing is unpacked to a temp folder first, so you no longer need room for the whole game on your temp drive.

- **exFAT, FFPKG and uncompressed PFS (`.ffpfs`)** are written in one pass through the archive.
- **Compressed images and packed folders** (zstd packs) are packed straight from the archive too; only the packs are written before the image is built from them. Compressed PFS (`.ffpfsc`) streams from a ZIP.
- The result is the same, byte for byte, as building from the unpacked folder, and every file's checksum is checked while it is read.
- FPKG packages still unpack the archive first (Sony's tools read a folder). The Build page tells you which way a build will go.

Building from a folder works exactly as before.

## Compressed exFAT, one click

The exFAT tile now starts with **Image type: Standard / Compressed**. Compressed is the same `.exfat` you already use, just smaller: the game's files go into zstd packs that the bundled ampr-emu-ng reads on the console. Keep your original dump; not every game runs packed yet.

## New: ZSTD image (experimental, #98)

A new format tile: one `.zstd` file (an exFAT image with the game in zstd packs) for Kraken Mount MOD. `.zstd` files also open in Image tools like any other image. ShadowMount+ does not mount the `.zstd` name: use Compressed exFAT for it.

## Newer engines and libraries

- **ampr-emu-ng 0.5.0** for zstd packs (was 0.3.3). The pack format is unchanged.
- **PS5 Backport engine 0.3.5-test4** on the Backport tab: Offline mode, clearer states ("Restore needed", "Needs SDK ≤ N"), a clearer Target SDK caption (#92), and Dump check now hands a game straight to the Backport tab (#26).
- **zlib 1.4 and LZ4 1.11.1**, the current releases, with their fixes for unpacking compressed data.

## From your reports

- **Sleep after the queue (#96):** an **Only after this run** switch next to "When the queue finishes". The action runs once, then goes back to Do nothing.
- **Package title (#94):** "Title for all languages" writes your title for every language of the game, so it shows whatever language the console is set to. The FPKG tile also takes ZIP, 7z and RAR dumps.
- **Folders (#90, #91):** Settings › Storage also lists the Backport tab's folders.

## Also

PFS images with very large folders are readable by more package builders; closing the app stops and records running jobs first, and asks while a PS5 tool or a backport run is still working; steadier FTP and kernel log in PS5 connect; interface fixes on every page; all new texts in the 42 languages.

Found something that does not work on your console? Please open an issue: they are read and answered.

# exFAT Image Builder 5 **Turn your PS5 game dumps into images that mount — and backport, convert, verify and send them to your console — from one app, in one download.** ![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%20%2F%2011%20x64-3d7bff) ![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/kerrdec97/ps5-exfat-builder?include_prereleases&color=8b5cf6) ![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/kerrdec97/ps5-exfat-builder/total?color=3d7bff) ![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-proprietary-8b5cf6) ![Home](docs/screenshots/home.png) > **Version 5 is a complete rewrite.** The app is now native C++/Qt: it > writes exFAT, UFS2 and PFS images itself, so it needs **no administrator > rights, no OSFMount, no .NET and no Python**, and it ships as **one .exe**. > > ⬇️ **Download 5.1.0** from the > [Releases page](https://github.com/kerrdec97/ps5-exfat-builder/releases): > one exe, nothing to install. > ⚠️ For games and content **you legally own and dumped yourself**. The app > does not download games, decrypt retail packages or bypass DRM, and it is > not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment. --- ## ✨ What it does | | | |---|---| | **Build image** | Drop a dump folder, or a ZIP, 7z or RAR of one (built straight from the archive, without unpacking it first), pick a format, done. **exFAT**, **FFPKG** (UFS2), **PFS** (compressed `.ffpfsc` or plain `.ffpfs`), installable **FPKG** `.pkg` (with your own Sony Publishing Tools; from a folder, any image or a packed game), or a **Packed folder** (no image: the game folder with its files in zstd packs, for a USB drive or FTP). Each output shows only its own options; experts get the rest under *Advanced options*. **Performance mode** (Low impact / Balanced / Maximum) on every format. Every image is read back and verified before it gets its final name, unless you turn verification off or cancel it (the job then says the image is not verified). | | **zstd packs** | *Compress game files*: the game's files go into zstd packs inside the image, served on the console by the bundled **ampr-emu-ng 0.5.0** runtime. Packed games (zstd or LZ4) are read through their packs everywhere: extract, convert, FPKG. Or skip the image: **Packed folder** packs the game folder itself. | | **Backport** | Make games run on older firmware with the built-in **PS5 Backport engine 0.3.5-test4 by Deckerr97** — the same engine as the standalone PS5 Backport GUI, so results are identical. Target SDK 4–13, PS5 Pro fix, PS5 Pro build, AMPR / PlayGo switch, and optional apply to the game folder with a verified originals backup and one-click restore. | | **Backport updates** | Ship a backport as its own small **update package** that installs over the game's base package, so the base stays the original game: Build image › FPKG › **Backport** (4.xx and/or 5.xx+ backport files, folder or ZIP). Each update is checked against the base before it gets its name. | | **DLC** | Turn DLC lists (`dlc_emu.ini` and other DLC INIs) and DLC `.pkg` files into installable PS5 DLC packages, retarget them to another region's game, and save updated INIs (needs your own fpkg-cli). | | **Image tools** | Open an image to **extract** it (packed games come out as plain files; an image inside an .ffpfsc is read straight through), **verify** it (or compare it with a folder), **convert** between exFAT, FFPKG, FFPFSC and FFPFS, or **edit** it (add, replace, rename, delete files). | | **PS5 connect** | A real FTP file manager with a transfer queue, payload sender, kernel log and crash-dump capture, **ShadowMount+ 1.7** configuration (new format, safe-to-unplug), Fakelib manager, autoloader, AMPR index, Y2JB tools (firmware → YouTube version table, one-click install from your own YouTube packages) and package install. | | **Library** | Your dumps and images in a cover-art grid: formats at a glance, bulk build, backport, rename. | | **Queue** | Everything runs in a queue you can pause, reorder, cancel and retry while you keep working. The page you start a job from turns into its monitor: every stage with its time, a live progress bar, speed and time left, and the job's log as it is written. |

## ⚡ Quick start 1. Download **`exFAT Image Builder.exe`** from the [Releases page](https://github.com/kerrdec97/ps5-exfat-builder/releases) and check its SHA-256 (below). 2. Run it. The first start unpacks the app once (a second or two); later starts are instant. 3. **Build image** → drop your game folder (the one with `eboot.bin`) → pick a format → **Build image**. Portable use: put an empty `portable.txt` next to the exe and the app keeps its settings, logs and unpacked files in that folder. Antivirus removes the exe? Download the **folder edition** (`exFAT-Image-Builder--win64-folder.zip`) from the same release instead: extract it anywhere and run the exe inside. It is the same program, already unpacked, so nothing unpacks itself on first start. ## 🔐 Verify your download Every release from 5.0.0 has `SHA256SUMS.txt`. In PowerShell: ```powershell Get-FileHash ".\exFAT.Image.Builder.exe" -Algorithm SHA256 ``` The download arrives as `exFAT.Image.Builder.exe`: GitHub replaces the spaces in the file name with dots. Compare the hash with the line in `SHA256SUMS.txt`; capital and small letters make no difference. ## 🛡 Antivirus warnings The exe is not code-signed and it is a self-extracting program (it unpacks the app and the backport engine to your user folder on first start), which some antivirus engines flag by heuristics (`Wacatac`, `!ml`). These are guesses, not matches. You can check the hash or scan it on VirusTotal. Please do not turn your protection off: [docs/ANTIVIRUS.md](docs/ANTIVIRUS.md) explains how to check your copy, use the folder edition and report a false positive to Microsoft or your antivirus vendor. Found a security problem? Please report it privately ([SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)). ## 🧰 Requirements * Windows 10 1809+ or Windows 11, 64-bit. * Optional: your own **Sony Publishing Tools** (`prospero-pub-cmd.exe`) for FPKG packages (backport updates need a verified SDK Fix release). Nothing from Sony is included or downloaded. * Optional: your own **fpkg-cli** (PSVIETHOA FPKG Builder, LibProsperoPkg by drakmor) for the DLC page. * For console features: a jailbroken PS5 running an FTP server (ftpsrv or etaHEN), and ShadowMount+ to mount images. ## Which PS5 firmware? * The builder runs on your PC and does not depend on your console's firmware: images and packages are built the same way for every firmware. * Whether they load on the console depends on its jailbreak and loader (etaHEN, ShadowMount+ and so on), not on this app. * A backport is only needed when a game's **Required FW** (shown on the Backport tab) is higher than your console's firmware. Otherwise build the game as it is. * On the Backport tab, **Target SDK** N gives a backport that loads on firmware N.00 and later; the default, SDK 4, loads on every firmware from 4.00. It cannot be higher than the game's own SDK. ## 🙏 Credits Created and maintained by **Deckerr97** ([@kerrdec97](https://github.com/kerrdec97)).
